title: What If the Panama Canal Ran Dry? It Nearly Did

scenes.text: What if the Panama Canal ran dry? In 2023, it nearly did.
Ships don't cross at sea level. Locks lift them 85 feet using fresh water, over 200 million liters for every crossing.
That is about 80 Olympic swimming pools, flushed out to sea, one ship at a time.
Then a drought hit. Daily crossings fell from about 36 a year earlier to 22, and ships queued for days.
In February 2024, Gatun Lake stood at 81 feet, its lowest level since 1965.
The canal carries about 6 percent of global sea trade. A dry lake means delays, higher costs, and long detours.

description:
What if the Panama Canal ran dry? In 2023, a drought forced it to cut crossings by a third.
Every ship uses over 200 million liters of fresh water, and the canal carries about 6 percent of world sea trade.
What should we run through next?
